title: भाषा शिक्षणमा उच्चारण शिक्षणको आवश्यकता, स्वरूप र प्रक्रिया Bhasha Shikshanma Ucchharan Shikshanko Aabashyakata, Swarup ra Prakriya
authors: पौडेल Poudel, माधव  Madhav प्रसाद Prasad
nepali: उच्चारण मूलतः बोलीसँग सम्बन्धित प्रक्रिया हो । यो सस्वर पठन÷वाचनकालागि पनि उत्तिकै महत्त्वपूर्ण र आधारभूत भाषिक प्रविधि हो । भाषा शिक्षणमा कथ्य वामौखिक भाषा र अभिव्यक्तिको व्यापक परिपोषण र सुधारका लागि उच्चारण शिक्षणअपरिहार्य आवश्यकता बनेको हुन्छ । कुनै पनि जीवन्त भाषा ध्वन्यात्मक रूपमै जीवितरहेको हुन्छ र त्यसैको तन्दुरुस्त उच्चारणका माध्यमले सम्प्रेषण सञ्चारको कार्य त्यसलेगरेको हुन्छ । वर्ण विन्यास वा हिज्जेले लेख्य भाषाको प्रतिनिधित्व गर्छ भने उच्चारणलेभाषाको कथ्य वा ध्वन्यात्मक रूपको प्रतिनिधित्व गरेको हुन्छ । संसारका कतिपयभाषाहरू अझै पनि ध्वन्यात्मक रूपमा मात्र जीवित छन् । त्यसैले कुनै पनि भाषाकोपहिलो र आधारभूत रूप भनेको त्यसको बोली हो र त्यही बोलीको प्रतिनिधित्व नैउच्चारण हो । लिप्यात्मक रूपमा चाहेर पनि सङ्केत गर्न नसकिने कतिपय खण्डीय वर्ण रभाषेतर पक्षको समेत हेक्का राखेर सोही अनुरूप उच्चारण गरी बोल्नु पर्ने भएकाले शिक्षणीयदृष्टिले यो लेख्य भाषाभन्दा जटिल र निरन्तर अभ्यास तथा प्रयोग अभ्यासका आधारमापरिमार्जित हुने खालको हुन्छ । सामाजिक र व्यावसायिक जीवनका दैनिक व्यवहारमाअत्यधिक प्रयोगमा कथ्य भाषाकै व्यवहार गरिने भएकाले जबसम्म सम्बन्धित भाषाकोउच्चारणमा अभ्यस्त भइँदैन तबसम्म भाषा सिकेको मान्न सकिँदैन । क्षेत्रीय, स्थानीय रविदेशी भाषाका उच्चारण प्रभाव तथा अन्य कतिपय कारणले उच्चारणमा अनेकौँ त्रुटिहरू हुनेगर्छन्, जसलाई राम्रोसँग पहिचान गरी तिनको सुधार र परिष्कार गर्नमा उच्चारण शिक्षणडोरिनु वा निर्देशित हुनु आवश्यक छ । यस लेखमा यसै दृष्टिकोणलाई मुख्य आधार बनाईभाषा शिक्षणमा उच्चारण शिक्षणको आवश्यकता, स्वरूप र प्रक्रियाहरूको खोजी गर्ने प्रयासगरिएको छ साथै नेपाली भाषा शिक्षणका सन्दर्भमा उच्चारण त्रुटिका कारण र त्रुटिक्षेत्रहरूकोसोदाहरण चिनारी गराउने प्रयत्न गरिनुका साथै शिक्षण कार्यकलाप र त्रुटि निराकरणकाउपायहरू पनि सुझाउने प्रयत्न गरिएको छ ।
american_english: Pronunciation is fundamentally a process associated with speech. It is an equally important and basic linguistic skill for oral reading and recitation. In language teaching, pronunciation instruction becomes an unavoidable necessity for the broad development and improvement of spoken language and expression. Any living language remains alive in its phonetic form itself, and it is through the correct pronunciation of that very language that it carries out the work of communication. Orthography or spelling represents written language, while pronunciation represents the spoken, or phonetic, form of language. Some languages of the world are still alive only in phonetic form. Therefore, the first and basic form of any language is its speech, and it is the representation of that speech which is pronunciation. Because certain regional sounds, which cannot be indicated even in written form, and the non-linguistic aspect must also be kept in mind, and one must speak by pronouncing in accordance with them, from a pedagogical point of view pronunciation is more complex than written language and is of the kind that is refined through constant practice and practice in use. Since it is spoken language that is used to the greatest extent in the daily dealings of social and professional life, until one is practised in the pronunciation of the language in question, one cannot be regarded as having learned the language. Owing to the influence of the pronunciation of regional, local and foreign languages, as well as several other factors, numerous errors occur in pronunciation, and pronunciation teaching must be properly guided in identifying them accurately and improving and refining them. In this article, taking this very standpoint as the main basis, an effort has been made to explore the necessity, nature and processes of pronunciation teaching in language teaching; alongside an effort to point out with examples the causes and areas of pronunciation errors in the context of Nepali language teaching, an effort has also been made to suggest classroom activities and remedies for correcting errors.
british_english: Pronunciation is, at root, a process bound up with speech. It is just as important and fundamental a linguistic skill for oral reading and recitation. In the teaching of language, pronunciation teaching becomes an indispensable requirement for the wide-ranging nurturing and improvement of spoken language and expression. Every living language remains alive in its phonetic form alone, and it is through the correct pronunciation of that same language that it performs the task of communication. Orthography, or spelling, represents written language, whereas pronunciation represents the spoken, or phonetic, form of a language. Certain of the world's languages remain alive in phonetic form only. Hence the first and fundamental form of any language is its speech, and it is the representation of that speech which constitutes pronunciation. Because certain regional sounds, which cannot be conveyed even by written means, together with the non-linguistic aspect, must be borne in mind, and because one is obliged to speak by pronouncing in keeping with them, pronunciation is, from a pedagogical point of view, more complex than written language and is of a kind that is honed through continual practice and practical exercise. Given that it is spoken language which is employed to the highest degree in the everyday transactions of social and professional life, one cannot be deemed to have learnt a language so long as one is not practised in the pronunciation of the language concerned. On account of the influence of the pronunciation of regional, local and foreign languages, as well as a number of other causes, many errors arise in pronunciation, and pronunciation teaching must be properly directed in identifying those errors accurately and in improving and refining them. In this article, taking this very perspective as its principal basis, an attempt has been made to examine the necessity, character and procedures of pronunciation teaching in language teaching; together with an attempt to illustrate, with examples, the causes and areas of pronunciation error in the context of the teaching of Nepali, an attempt has also been made to propose teaching activities and remedies for the correction of errors.
australian_english: Pronunciation is basically a process to do with speech. It is just as important and basic a language skill for reading aloud and recitation. In language teaching, teaching pronunciation becomes an absolute must for developing spoken language and expression broadly and improving them. Any living language stays alive in its sound form itself, and it is through the right pronunciation of that same language that it does the job of communicating. Spelling or orthography stands for written language, while pronunciation stands for the spoken or sound form of a language. Quite a few of the world's languages are still alive only as sounds. So the first and most basic form of any language is its spoken form, and pronunciation is what represents that spoken form. Since some regional sounds cannot be shown even in writing, and the non-language side of things has to be kept in mind too, and you have got to speak by pronouncing in line with them, pronunciation is trickier than written language from a teaching point of view, and it is the sort of thing that gets polished up through constant practice and practice in actual use. Given that it is spoken language that gets used the most in the everyday dealings of social and working life, you cannot say you have learned a language until you are practiced in pronouncing it. Because of the pull of how regional, local and foreign languages are pronounced, plus a number of other reasons, lots of mistakes crop up in pronunciation, and teaching pronunciation needs to be properly guided in picking out those mistakes accurately and fixing and refining them. In this article, using this same angle as the main foundation, there is an attempt to look into the need, the nature and the processes of pronunciation teaching in language teaching; as well as an attempt to point out, with examples, the causes of pronunciation mistakes and the mistake-prone areas in the context of teaching Nepali, there is also an attempt to suggest teaching activities and ways of correcting mistakes.
